## e2627920c372

**Reproduced defect and shortcut.** Generator SHA `536523d088cca4b6e49efcc36e95a931c65b61a876a478953fd4dc3361c73fe3`; executed rule hash `ba3c5705c8fe`.

The generator always places the transform-control code at `(0,0)`, and `self_check` rejects a control anywhere else even though the published invariants only require one legal control marker. All five official canonical inputs are rejected with `default control marker should be at (0,0)`. Thus the generated domain excludes the canonical placement variation and supports the shortcut “read a control only at the top-left.”

`checks/audit/e2627920c372/counterexample.json` uses official canonical `train[1]`, whose code 3 is at `(8,1)`. The input belongs to the documented/canonical task domain but does **not** pass this target’s validator. A rival that ignores non-top-left controls and defaults to identity stamps a different shape than the canonical Racket output. `racket.json` records supported execution and the exact input/output/rule/generator hashes; `rival_output.json` is the conflicting identity-stamp result.

No target files were changed.
